title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Alicia Romero
description: Motivation: production traffic patterns exposed cases where the continuous-batcher scheduler favored throughput at the cost of request-level fairness. Small, latency-sensitive requests experienced starvation behind long-lived large batches on some GPU pools; in other pools tail latency degraded under bursty arrival patterns. This PR adds scheduler tuning to improve queueing fairness, prevent starvation, and introduce adaptive timeouts while preserving overall throughput. Summary of changes: 1) introduced per-queue aging and dynamic priority boosts so older requests gain scheduling weight over time; 2) added a configurable max-queue-time and per-request adaptive timeout heuristic that tightens timeouts for long-running batches and relaxes them for short requests to reduce unnecessary cancellations; 3) switched from a single global enqueue ordering to a bucketed queue keyed by expected token-length and priority-class to reduce head-of-line blocking from very long sequences; 4) added backpressure signals to the router so upstream load-balancers can shift requests away from overloaded pools earlier; 5) instrumented new metrics (queue_age_{p50,p95}, starvation_events, adaptive_timeout_adjustments, bucket_fill_ratio) and added Grafana panels and alert rules for starvation and queue growth; 6) added deterministic unit tests and integration canary that simulates mixed short/long workloads to validate fairness across different load shapes. Backwards compatibility: scheduler defaults preserve current behavior unless feature flags are set; parameters exposed as runtime-config with safe defaults. Performance: in internal perf lab the changes reduced 99th percentile request latency for short requests by ~28% under mixed workloads and eliminated observed starvation events across 4/5 canary pools. Related work: builds on prior continuous-batcher scheduler improvements (see ENG-3890) and complements kernel-level batching changes in pr-67245. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in ENG-4321 - [x] Feature-flagged rollout path - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Perf benchmark and canary results included - [x] Grafana/alerting panels added - [x] Docs/console descriptions for the tunables Files touched include scheduler core, queueing policy, router backpressure, config schema, metrics, tests, and docs. Requesting review from runtime and infra leads for validation of pool-level defaults and alert thresholds.
